one_line: Early Upanishadic philosopher from Videha who challenges Yajnavalkya in King Janaka’s court.

appearance.age_look: Late 20s to early 30s, slim but sturdy build, poised with a quiet intensity.
appearance.face: Oval face, medium brown Mithila complexion, straight nose, sharp dark eyes with a thoughtful gaze, high cheekbones, a small tilak of simple pale yellow sandal paste on the forehead, default expression calm but keenly inquisitive as if about to ask a question.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair parted in the middle and drawn back into a single long braid reaching mid-back, braid wrapped at intervals with narrow off-white cotton threads; a simple narrow dark brown headband of woven plant fibre sits low on the forehead, keeping stray strands in place.
appearance.costume: Era-appropriate simple scholar’s attire: a full-length undyed off-white cotton sari-style lower garment (wrapped once around the waist and falling to the ankles, plain woven with a faint narrow brown border), paired with a separate knee-length upper cloth of the same fabric draped diagonally over the left shoulder and across the torso, fully covering the chest and back; beneath the drape a short-sleeved fitted blouse-like inner tunic in muted ochre-brown, visible at the upper arms and neckline; she wears a plain dark brown woven cotton waistband tightening the lower wrap, small round wooden bead earrings, a single thin copper bangle on each wrist, and simple leather sandals with toe loops.
appearance.signature: A smooth dark brown wooden staff (about chin-height) with subtle carved ring markings near the top, carried in her right hand, plus a small rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a thin cord tucked at her waist on the left side.

ref_desc: Gargi Vachaknavi is a medium-brown, oval-faced woman in her early thirties with sharp dark eyes, long black braided hair with cotton wraps and a simple headband, wearing an off-white wrapped sari and ochre-brown inner tunic with minimal wooden and copper ornaments, carrying a dark brown wooden staff and a small palm-leaf manuscript, in a palette of off-white, muted ochre-brown, dark brown, copper and black.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Gargi Vachaknavi, early Upanishadic philosopher in King Janaka’s Videha court: a late-20s to early-30s woman of medium brown Mithila complexion, oval face, sharp dark eyes, thoughtful calm expression and a small pale sandal paste tilak; her thick black hair is center-parted and pulled into a single long braid to mid-back, the braid wrapped at intervals with narrow off-white threads, held in place by a simple narrow dark brown woven headband low on the forehead. She wears historically plausible c. 700–600 BCE north Indian scholar’s clothing: a full-length undyed off-white cotton sari-like lower wrap with a faint narrow brown border, wrapped once around the waist and falling to the ankles; an upper cloth of the same off-white cotton draped diagonally over the left shoulder and across the torso, entirely covering chest and back; beneath that a modest short-sleeved fitted inner tunic in muted ochre-brown visible at the sleeves and neckline; a plain dark brown woven cotton waistband securing the lower wrap. Add minimal jewellery: small round wooden bead earrings, a single thin copper bangle on each wrist, and simple brown leather sandals with toe loops. Her signature prop is a smooth dark brown wooden staff about chin height with carved ring markings near the top in her right hand, and a small rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a cord tucked at her left waist. Use a restrained palette of off-white, muted ochre-brown, dark brown, copper and black, and pose her neutrally, front and slight angle views, to clearly show face, braid, garments, staff and manuscript bundle for consistent redrawing.
